# $exists query bounds on indexes — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for $exists query bounds on indexes. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-21 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] An all-ascending/descending compound sparse index includes a document when at least one indexed key has a value. Index membership therefore does not by itself prove that every individual component exists; the exact sparse-index claim above is limited to a single-field index. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md

## How it works

- [statement] $exists:true matches documents where the field is present, including an explicit null value; $exists:false matches only documents where the field is absent. A null equality query is different because it also matches missing fields. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-21) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: $exists query bounds on indexes · also: https://dev.to/franckpachot/exists-and-non-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb-and-in-other-documentdb-19e3

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A sparse index on f cannot answer {f: {$exists: false}} because it omits the matching missing-field documents, so MongoDB requires a COLLSCAN for that index. A non-sparse index can scan the null-key candidates and use FETCH to distinguish absent fields from explicitly-null fields; the optimizer may still prefer a collection scan. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: $exists query bounds on indexes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md, https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79734755/can-mongodb-use-an-index-for-exists-false-on-an-indexed-field/79734804, https://dev.to/franckpachot/exists-and-non-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb-and-in-other-documentdb-19e3, https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-12869
- [statement] A partial index filtered by {f: {$exists: true}} only covers documents where f exists. MongoDB uses a partial index only when the query implies its filter, so that index cannot answer {f: {$exists: false}} without omitting matches. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md · keywords: $exists query bounds on indexes · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/using-partial-and-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For a single-field sparse index on f, {f: {$exists: true}} can use the full [MinKey, MaxKey] range as an exact existence test: missing fields have no index entries, but explicit null values do. MongoDB does not need a FETCH just to recheck existence, though it may fetch documents to return fields that are not covered by the index. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: $exists query bounds on indexes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md, https://dev.to/franckpachot/exists-and-non-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb-and-in-other-documentdb-19e3, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/query/plan_enumerator/README.md, https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-sparse-index/markdown
- [statement] A non-sparse single-field index stores a null-like key for documents missing f. Therefore, {f: {$exists: true}} has no selective value bound from existence alone: an observed IXSCAN spans [MinKey, MaxKey] and FETCH applies the $exists filter, examining all index entries and documents. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: $exists query bounds on indexes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/using-partial-and-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb/, https://dev.to/franckpachot/exists-and-non-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb-and-in-other-documentdb-19e3, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/query/plan_enumerator/README.md
